parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM-only .mjs output, manual process.argv parsing, no external dependencies, local module split, exact stdout/stderr and exit-code behavior, and black-box executable probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership while delegating CLI behavior probing to a first-level child, which further delegated executable probing to a nested child. Parent retained final assembly and verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Parent created separate CLI modules for program naming, messages, parser, a CLI index, schedule job/index modules, and test3.mjs; implementation handled required args, help, invalid ints, unknown extras, repeated flags, inline values, negative ints, and -- handling.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote all final files under /output and artifact validation captured test3.mjs plus the local CLI and schedule modules. Child work was not integrated as source code.
parallel.verification: Parent compared executable behavior and Node output across representative cases, then ran a normalized batch comparison that exited with no mismatch output. Official evaluation passed 70 of 70.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No user-visible task defect remained at closure, but the first-level probe child was still running and was explicitly interrupted before returning its own final handoff.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual parser, zero-dependency, local-module, exact argparse behavior, output alignment, and executable-observation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned probing, parser design, schedule facade, final assembly, verification, and delivery without delegation or handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: Serial created path-utils.mjs, cli/test3-args.mjs, schedule/job.mjs, schedule/index.mjs, and test3.mjs; it implemented argparse-like option matching, value consumption, int parsing, repr formatting, and schedule interval printing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial assembled one coherent /output tree with test3.mjs as the entrypoint and all imports using explicit .mjs suffixes; artifact validation accepted the final tree.
serial.verification: Serial probed many executable edge cases, ran Node against the same cases, fixed replaceAll portability, and reran a normalized comparison harness successfully. Official evaluation passed 70 of 70.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation or official defect is visible in the completed serial run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual CLI parsing, no-external-dependency, local module split, and exact output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and probed the executable to match argparse edge cases and printed interval behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both solved the same required behavior and passed the same official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent delegated CLI probing to a child and nested child but kept parent-side ownership of implementation, assembly, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor own probing, implementation, assembly, testing, and final response without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child lifecycle boundaries and redundant probing; serial was linear and had no handoff or child lifecycle surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children had the original prompt context and returned probe information, but final source interfaces were parent-owned local ESM imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial designed its module interfaces locally with explicit .mjs imports and no cross-agent handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The module boundaries differed in naming and granularity, but neither trajectory shows a missing or incompatible interface contract in the delivered artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent implemented a multi-file CLI/parser/message layout plus a schedule Job facade and entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a path utility, one consolidated CLI parser module, a schedule builder/job pair, and an entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementations covered the same observable behavior through different internal module layouts; neither layout caused an official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The nested child completed a probe report and the parent could see it in list_agents, but the first-level child stayed running and was explicitly interrupted before its own final return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; local implementation and verification completed in one timeline before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only the parallel run had an adverse result lifecycle event, but it did not change the official outcome because the parent had already completed the solution path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent wrote the final /output tree and artifact validation captured one coherent set of files; children did not land competing source changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and delivered a coherent /output tree from a single writer, with no concurrent shared-state surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used shared workspace capability but did not show a collision or overwrite; serial avoided the risk by not delegating.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent ran targeted Node checks and a normalized comparison harness, then official evaluation passed 70 of 70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran the same style of targeted checks, fixed a portability concern, reran a normalized comparison harness, and official evaluation passed 70 of 70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification depth was materially similar, with both attempts confirming representative CLI behavior before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more total tokens and tool calls, waited twice on the probe child, interrupted it, and still closed with a passing final answer in 261.735 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout with no subagents, more elapsed agent seconds but fewer tokens, and closed after successful comparison and final code presentation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget on redundant child work and an interrupted child lifecycle, while serial spent budget linearly; neither run timed out or failed acceptance.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official completed status records report solution_passed true with 70 of 70 samples passed. The parallel run's coordination difference was redundant delegated probing and an interrupted first-level child, while the parent still implemented and verified the required artifact. The serial run solved the same task through a single-agent implementation path. There is no discordant official outcome to explain.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation and verification carried the solution despite the interrupted child.
Nested child produced a probe report, but final correctness did not depend on integrating child source code.
serial_contributors: Single agent probed executable behavior, implemented local ESM modules, patched one portability detail, and verified against the executable.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel split CLI behavior into prog-name, messages, parser, and index modules; serial consolidated most CLI behavior into test3-args.mjs plus path-utils.mjs.
Both layouts were accepted by artifact validation and official tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process event only

candidates.reason: Parent directly implemented the required /output modules, and the child also pursued implementation, so implementation was not ownerless.
No separately completed child components required reconciliation; the parent owned the final integrated module tree.
Parent assembled test3.mjs and all library files under /output, and artifact validation found the expected entrypoint.
Parent covered probing, implementation, verification, and final delivery; the interrupted child did not leave the end-to-end pipeline ownerless.
Executable probing informed both runs, but parallel work was not blocked behind a mandatory single preflight that caused unfinished implementation.
Parallel parent and children overlapped probing, and the parent completed implementation and verification normally rather than deferring all productive work until too late.
The indispensable implementation and verification path stayed with the parent and completed successfully; no critical path was starved by auxiliary child work.
The run spawned only a small probe chain, did not exhaust the cell budget, did not time out, and passed all official samples.
The first-level child was interrupted while still running, but there is no direct evidence that an overbroad child scope caused indispensable work to remain unfinished.
The child trajectory included the original task prompt context, and no omitted known requirement in a child brief caused unusable final work.

The returned probe report was long but did not prevent the parent from completing implementation or verification within the decision window.
No handoff described a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state that caused rework or invalid verification.
The reviewed child and parent findings were not incompatible at a decision point, and no unresolved conflicting contracts blocked integration.
Parent performed representative verification before final response, and no visible unresolved integrated acceptance gap remained before closure.
The nested probe was not an observed replacement retry of failed work lacking checkpoints, and no checkpoint-free repeated failure occurred.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Parent interrupted the active first-level probe child after the child had continued probing and announced module-writing work, before that child produced its own final handoff.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active first-level child produced no own final handoff, leaving its probe and intended implementation branch redundant and unusable by the final parent-owned solution.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent had already implemented and verified the required solution, so no required failed child scope was abandoned without takeover.

candidates.reason: The final deliverable was written, verified, and accepted before closure; no complete candidate was left unpromoted or unpackaged.
No child implementation change was merged after integrated verification; parent verification followed the parent-written files.
The interrupted child did not complete a retrievable implementation for the parent to join, and the nested child only returned behavior probes.
The nested probe result reached the first-level child and was visible in parent list_agents output; the retained issue is the first-level child's interruption, not a trapped verifier finding.
Although a child was interrupted, the parent had already taken over the implementation and verification path and no required scope remained unowned.
Parent inspected child state with list_agents and the completed nested probe was not a first-level completed implementation result that the parent ignored inconsistently.
Parent waits were bounded and followed by list_agents inspections, not blind waiting until the overall deadline or timeout.
No live child wrote a competing implementation path or incompatible file set; the parent-owned output tree was coherent.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source or configuration file and reconciling a concurrent change.
No actor replaced or deleted source produced or owned by another actor; children did not land final source changes.
No child-produced entrypoint or submitted artifact was overwritten by another live actor; parent created the delivered test3.mjs.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
The reviewed child trajectories did not write shared implementation files, and no unstable-state or provenance problem resulted from workspace sharing.
No generated file, fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed as stable input by another actor.
